Setting up of NIPER  
 
2463. SHRI PATEL HASMUKHBHAI SOMABHAI:  
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has approved any proposal for any setting up of National Institute 
of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER) in Gujarat State;  
(b) if so, the time by which it is likely to be opened along with the outlay for setting up of the 
NIPER in Gujarat State;  
(c) the details of NIPER established in the country at present, State-wise; and  
(d) the details of the total cost involved in this regard, year-wise?

MINISTER IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS  
(SHRI D.V. SADANANADA GOWDA) 
 
(a) & (b) The Government has already set up a National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education 
and Research (NIPER ) at Ahmedabad, Gujarat in the year 2007. The institute is currently 
functioning from a transient, temporary building on a 60-acre site at Gandhinagar, Gujarat since 
August 2016. It offers masters and doctorate courses in eight different specializations of  
pharmaceuticals and medical devices. More than 600 students have already graduated from the 
Institute and are well placed in various pharma industries in India and abroad.  
 
(c)      At present, seven NIPERs have been established at NIPER SAS Nagar, Mohali (Punjab), 
NIPER Ahmedabad (Gujarat), NIPER Guwahati (Assam), NIPER Hajipur (Bihar), NIPER 
Hyderabad (Telangana), NIPER Kolkata (West Bengal) and NIPER Raebareli (Uttar Pradesh).

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY & DAIRYING 
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 2464 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 9th MARCH, 2021 
 
FISHERIES MANAGEMENT FRAMEWORK 
 
2464: SHRI LALLU SINGH:  
 
 Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY & DAIRYING मत्स्यपालन, 
पशुपालन और डेयरी मंत्री be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has formulated any plan to diligently explore the resources available 
in the country such as waterlogged areas, wetlands, lakes, canals, ponds, backwaters, lagoons 
etc. for increasing the fish production; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c) the details of the steps taken by the Government to establish a robust fisheries management 
framework as well as for improving socio -economic condition of fishermen and other people 
associated with the sector? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING: 
 
(SHRI PRATAP CHANDRA SARANGI) 
 
(a) and (b): Yes sir. The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and 
Dairying is implementing a flagship scheme namely “Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana  
(PMMSY)”- to bring about Blue Revolution through sustainable and responsible development of 
fisheries sector in India ” with highest ever investment of Rs. 20050 crore in fisheries sector for a 
period of 5 years with effect from the financial year 2020 -21. PMMSY inter alia provides support 
for promoting of aquaculture in  waterlogged areas, wetlands, lakes, canals, ponds, backwaters, 
lagoons etc. for increasing the fish production . The activities taken up in such water -bodies 
primarily includes stocking of fingerlings, pen culture, cage culture, setting up of in-situ hatcheries, 
facilities for post-harvest handling and fish marketing. 
(c):  The PMMSY provides for establishment of a robust fisheries management framework and 
in this regard it provides need-based support to States/UTs for formulation and implementation of 
fisheries management plans . Besides, the PMMSY promotes aquaculture, mariculture an d post 
harvest management and also various economic activities in fisheries, aiming towards 
enhancement of income and improve socio -economic condition of fishers and other stakeholders 
associated with fisheries sector.

SMART POLICE STATION SCHEME 
 
†2469. SHRI GOPAL CHINNAYA SHETTY: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government proposes to include all the States of the country 
under Smart Police Station Scheme; and 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the action being taken in this regard? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
(SHRI G. KISHAN REDDY) 
 
(a) & (b) 'Public Order' and 'Police' being State subjects as per the 
Constitution of India, the principal responsibility of modernisation of Police 
Stations lies with the State Governments. There is no scheme named ‘Smart 
Police Station Scheme’, however, under the scheme of ‘Assistance to States 
for Modernisation of Police’, the Government of India provides assistance for 
acquiring modern gadgets and weaponry for police stations as per the 
proposal of State Governments.

Productions by farmers happen based on local agro

marketing and value chain infrastructure by private sector including that by private corporate

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF PHARMACEUTICALS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. †2473 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 9th March, 2021 
 
Price of Medicines 
 
†2473. SHRI CHIRAG KUMAR PASWAN:  
 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the prices of medicines are higher in the country as compared to the neighbouring 
countries;  
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;  
(c) whether any concrete steps have been taken by the Government to reduce the pr ices of 
medicines; and  
(d) if so, the details and achievement thereof along with the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
(SHRI D.V. SADANANADA GOWDA) 
 
(a) to (b): No information regarding prices of medicines in neighbouring countries is 
readily available. However, the prices of medicines in the country are not high and the same 
are regulated as per provisions of the Drug Prices Control Orders (DPCOs) issued from tim e 
to time.      
 
(c) to (d): The medicines which are covered under the National List of Essential Medicines 
(NLEM) announced by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare are included in the Schedule 
– I of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013 (DPCO, 2013) and the ceiling price of these 
medicines are fixed by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) under the 
Department of Pharmaceuticals. The details of medicines under price control are as under: 
 
 NPPA has fixed the ceiling prices of 881 schedul ed formulations of medicines under 
NLEM, 2015.  
 NPPA has also fixed the retail price of 1,495 new drugs under DPCO, 2013. 
 NPPA fixed prices of 106 Anti -diabetic and Cardiovascular drugs under Para 19 of 
DPCO, 2013 in Public interest. NPPA has fixed ceiling  price of Cardiac Stents being 
scheduled formulation under DPCO, 2013 affecting price reduction for Coronary Stents 
worked out up to 85% for Bare Metal Stents and 74% for Drug Eluting Stents. 
 NPPA has fixed ceiling price of Orthopedic Knee Implants under P ara 19 of DPCO, 
2013 in Public interest affecting price reduction for orthopedic Knee Implants worked 
out up to be 69%. 

 NPPA capped the Trade Margin of non-scheduled formulations of 42 select Anti-cancer 
medicines under “Trade Margin Rationalization” appro ach as a Pilot for proof of 
concept, wherein price of above 500 brands of medicines were reduced upto 90%. 
 
The fixation of prices has resulted in a total saving of Rs. 12,447 crores per annum to the public 
after implementation of DPCO, 2013.

2475.  DR. VIRENDRA KUMAR: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the targets set and roads constructed in kilom eters under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak 
Yojana(PMGSY) during the last three years, State-wise including Madhya Pradesh; and 
(b)  the names of agencies which have been awarded construction work of these roads under 
the said scheme and the State-level officers responsible for ensuring the quality/criteria of 
roads and maintenance, State-wise?  
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a) Under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY),  details of target set and roads 
constructed in kilometers during the last three yea rs, State-wise including Madhya Pradesh are given 
at Annexure-I.  
 
(b)       The names of agencies which have been awa rded construction work of above roads under 
PMGSY can be seen on PMGSY website URL http://omms. nic.in >Proposals>State-wise List of 
Roads. 
 
PMGSY envisages a three tier Quality Assurance Mechanism to ensure quality of road works 
during construction. First-tier of this mechanism i s in-house quality control at Programme 
Implementation Unit (PIU) level. Second-tier is str uctured as an independent quality monitoring at 
State level through State Quality Monitors (SQMs) i n which provision of regular inspection of 
PMGSY works has been envisaged. The third-tier is a n independent monitoring mechanism at the 
Central level. Under this tier, independent Nationa l Quality Monitors (NQMs) are engaged for 
inspections of PMGSY roads, selected at random. Act ion Taken Reports of the road works graded as 
Satisfactory Requiring Improvement (SRI) and Unsati sfactory (U) by the State Quality Monitors are 
monitored by the respective State Governments.  Sim ilarly, for works graded as Satisfactory 
Requiring Improvement (SRI) and Unsatisfactory (U) on the basis of observations of National 
Quality Monitors, Action Taken Reports are monitore d and processed by National Rural 
Infrastructure Development Agency (NRIDA). 
Further, ensuring the quality of the road works is the responsibility of the State Governments, who 
are implementing the Programme. The State Quality C oordinators (SQCs) of the respective States 
have been designated as Nodal Officers for ensuring  the quality and maintenance of roads under the 
PMGSY.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRYAND DAIRYING  
DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2478 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 9TH MARCH, 2021 
 
PROMOTION OF FISHERIES IN NALANDA 
 
2478.  SHRI KAUSHALENDRA KUMAR: 
 
Will the Minist er of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING  
मत्स्यपाऱन, पशुपाऱन और डेयरी मंत्री be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that an awareness about fisheries is 
increasing in the State of Bihar, particularly in Nalanda district; 
 
(b) whether the Nalanda district of the State of Bihar has the first position in fisheries;  
 
(c) the details of incentives being provided by the Government to the farmers so as to 
promote fisheries;  
 
(d) whether the Government is also considering to provide interest free loan to fisheries 
farmers; 
 
(e) whether the Government is considering to provide special economic assistance to the 
farmers keeping in view high water requirement and high cost of diesel in fisheries; 
and  
 
(f) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRYAND DAIRYING 
(SHRI PRATAP CHANDRA SARANGI) 
(a) and (b) :  The Government of Bihar has reported that awareness towards fish farming has 
been increased throughout the State including Nalanda District through seminars, workshops 
and training programmes. Fish farming is  becoming popular with the introduction of various 
schemes of Government of India and State plan schemes.  It is further reported that Nalanda 
District is one of the fisheries potential districts of the State.  
(c) to (f) :  The Department of Fisheries,  Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and 
Dairying is implementing a flagship scheme “Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana 

(PMMSY) - A scheme to bring about Blue Revolution through sustainable and responsible 
development of fisheries sector in India ” with highest ever estimate investment of Rs.20050 
crore in fisheries sector for a period of 5 years with effect from the financial year 2020 -21. 
The financial assistance provided under PMMSY to fish farmers includes, construction of 
ponds with inputs cost, Re-circulatory Aquaculture System(RAS), hatcheries for quality seed 
supply, feed plants, biofloc aquaculture units, cold storages, transport and marketing 
facilities, value added facilities,  cage culture and pen culture units, support for ornament al 
fish culture, integrated fish farming, recreational fisheries etc.   During the current financial 
year (2020 -21), the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying  has accorded 
approval to the proposal of Government of Bihar at  a total cost of Rs. 107.00 crore under the 
PMMSY.  Besides, the Department of Fisheries,  Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry 
and Dairying is also implementing Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development 
Fund (FIDF) with the fund size of Rs. 7522 crores for concessional  financing to Eligible 
Entities (EEs)  including fish farmers for development of identified fisheries infrastructure 
facilities.

2479.  SHRIMATI HARSIMRAT KAUR BADAL: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has instituted any enqu iry into the irregularities and frauds 
committed by Punjab Government officials in defraying Mahatma Gandhi National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) funds; 
(b) if so, whether any report has been submitted in  this regard; 
(c)  whether any chargesheet has been prepared for alleged siphoning of crores of funds under 
fake names and identities by officials and if so, the details thereof; 
(d)  the action initiated by the Government in this  regard; 
(e)  whether the Government proposes to file crimin al charges against all those involved in this 
scam and if so, the details thereof; and 
(f)  if not, the reasons therefor?  
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a) to (f): Yes, Madam. Complaints received in the Ministry are forwarded to the concerned 
States/Union Territories (UTs) for taking appropriate action including investigation. In some cases, 
Central Team, special National Monitors are also se nt for investigation into the matter. Steps have 
been taken to strengthen transparency and accountab ility which include geo-tagging of assets, 
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), National electronic Fund Management System (Ne-FMS), Aadhaar 
Based Payment System (ABPS), Software for Estimate Calculation using Rural rates for 
Employment (SECURE) and establishment of independen t social audit units and appointment of 
Ombudspersons in the States/UTs. Also State/UT spec ific reviews are undertaken from time to 
time.  
On receipt of a complaint related to State Governme nt of Punjab, a Central Team under the 
leadership of senior officer has been deputed for i nvestigation of the complaint. A detailed enquiry 
report was sent to the State for Action Taken Repor t (ATR). On recommendation of enquiry 
Committee, State Government has taken several steps  such as recovery from responsible officers 
as well as disciplinary action. First Information Report (FIR) has been lodged against Gram Rojgar 
Sahayak (GRS) by District administration. In this regard, details are given at Annexure.   
 
In another complaint related to State of Punjab, NL M team was sent twice, but no 
significant irregularities were found.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 09/03/2021 
 
 
PROMOTE INDIGENOUS VARIETIES OF RICE 
 
 
2494. SHRI JASBIR SINGH GILL:  
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE    
d`f"k vkSj fdlku dY;k.k ea=h be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has formulated any plan or scheme to promote indigenous 
varieties of rice and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b) whether the  Government is aware that some indigenous varieties of rice have low 
glycemic index (GI) and are beneficial for diabetics and if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c) the steps taken/being taken by the Government to promote such varieties of rice;  
 
(d) whether the Government has imposed any charge for GI certification and if so, the 
details thereof;  
 
(e) whether the Government has listed indigenous varieties of rice that are currently 
being grown in India; and  
 
(f) if so, the details thereof? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
d`f”k vkSj fdlku dY;k.k ea=h                               (SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a)  
• Indigenous varieties of rice are being promoted through varieties programmes. 574 
indigenous varieties of rice have bee n propagated and tested at more than 10,000 farmers’ 
fields, involving state agricultural universities, KVKs and NGOs through a project entitled 
“Mainstreaming Agricultural biodiversity conservation and utilization of the agriculture 
sector to ensure ecosy stem services and reduce vulnerability”.  Nutritional profiling of 
300 selected rice varieties has been done for market linkage and better price to the 
farmers. Farmers are also being trained on conservation, improvement and use of 
traditional/ indigenous varieties through participatory variety selection. Further for access 
to seeds of these indigenous varieties, community seed banks have been established at 

2 
 
community level involving KVKs and Self Help Groups in remote and tribal areas of the 
country and a  total of 26 community seed banks conserving >4000 native landraces and 
farmers’ varieties of different food crops including rice have been strengthened and 
established.  
• Communities and farmers conserving and promoting indigenous rice varieties have been 
conferred with Genome Savour awards by Protection of Plant Varieties Protection and 
Farmers’ Rights Authority  (PPV&FRA) and following awards have been given since 
2009-10: 
a. Plant Genome Saviour Community Award (Rs. 10 lakh each ): 13 
b. Plant Genome Saviour Farmer Rewards (Rs. 1.5 lakhs each): 12 
c. Plant Genome Saviour Farmer Recognitions (Rs. 1.0 lakh each): 19   
• Rice varieties are also being promoted under National Food Security Mission in 193 
districts of 24 states and Union Territory. Similarly,  “Bringing Gree n Revolution to 
Eastern India (BGREI)”  a sub scheme of Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana   is implemented 
in seven Eastern States viz., Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Eastern 
Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal to address the constraints limiting the productivity of “rice 
based cropping systems” in Eastern India. 
 
(b) & (c): Yes, five rice varieties viz.,  Lalat and Improved Lalat (GI value: 54) as low GI 
and Swarna, Sambha Mahsuri and Shaktiman (GI value  <60) as intermediate GI have been 
identified and all these varieties are in seed chain and are being cultivated by the farmers. 
 
(d) There is no certification for GI (Glycemic Index) in rice. 
 
(e) & (f): Yes, the details of indigenous rice varieties/ germplasm listed are as under: 
 
Total rice germplasm conserved at National Gene Bank:  1,09,834 including traditional 
varieties (6,707), land races (38400) and varieties released and notified (1190). 
Varieties registered with PPV&FRA:  Total 2047 varieties have been registered which 
include 1645 farmers varieties.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2495 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 09TH MARCH, 2021/ PHALGUNA 18, 1942 (SAKA) 
 
SOCIAL SECURITY SCHEMES TO PRISONERS 
 
2495.     DR. (PROF.) KIRIT PREMJIBHAI SOLANKI: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has formulated any Social security scheme(s) 
applicable to prisoners and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether the Government has formulated any social security scheme(s) 
applicable to women prisoners and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c) whether the Government has formulated any social security scheme(s) 
applicable to the children of prisoners, outside the prison and if so, the 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI G. KISHAN REDDY) 
 
(a) to (c): ‘Prisons’ and ‘persons detained therein’ are ‘State’ subjects as 
per Entry 4 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India. 
The State Governments are competent to devise and implement 
appropriate social security schemes for prison inmates, including women 
prisoners and children of prisoners etc., and for employment oriented skill 
development programmes for their re-integration into the society upon 
release.  The  Ministry of Home Affairs has issued advisories to States  and  
 
 

 
-2- 
L.S.US.Q.NO.2495 FOR 09.03.2021 
 
UTs on efficient Prison Administration and for providing vocational and 
skill development training to prisoners, including women inmates. The 
Ministry of Home Affairs had also advised the States and UTs to 
coordinate and collaborate with their Skill Development Departments and 
to make provision for suitable opportunities for the development of skills 
of prison inmates, particularly women prisoners, to facilitate their 
reintegration into the society by providing them post release employment 
opportunities. States and UTs have also been advised to formulate 
suitable schemes and develop policy for providing employment to released 
convicts. States have been advised that on release from prisons, individual 
cases of released prisoners may be followed up by the concerned 
Probation/Welfare/Rehabilitation Officers for a period ranging from one 
year to five years according to the requirement of each case and the 
status of their rehabilitation and reintegration into the society may be 
closely monitored at appropriate level.  
Model Prison Manual, 2016 forwarded to all States and UTs, has specific 
chapters on ‘Vocational training and skill development programmes’, 
‘After-Care and Rehabilitation’ and ‘Women Prisoners’ etc. The guidelines 
contained in these chapters provide detailed guidance to the States about 
the rehabilitation and reintegration of prison inmates.

(c) the details of utilized/unutilized funds under various schemes of FPI sector during  the 
last three years, State-wise?  
 
 ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAMESWAR TELI) 
  
(a) to (c): Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) is implementing  Central Sector 
umbrella scheme - PRADHAN MANTRI KISAN SAMPADA YOJANA (PMKSY) for overall 
growth and development of food processing sector across the country (including the State of 
Jharkhand). The scheme components of  PMKSY are demand driven, under which credit linked 
capital subsidy in the form of grant-in-aid is provided to eligible applicants. The Scheme wise 
allocations made under PMKSY and funds utilized during last three years(2017 -18, 2018-19 
and 2019-20) and the current financial year i.e. 2020-21 (till 26.02.2021) is placed at Annexure. 
 
Also, as part of Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan, MoFPI has launched an all India 
centrally sponsored "PM Formalization of Micro food processing Enterprises (PMFME)

MGNREGS IN ODISHA 
 
2499.  SHRI. RAMESH CHANDRA MAJHI: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has identified the work s which can be executed under the 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) in 
Odisha; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  the details of the estimated amount for this w ork; and 
(d)  the details of the targets fixed in this regar d and the time by which it is likely to be 
started?  
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR) 
 
(a) to (d):      Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma 
Gandhi NREGS) is a demand driven wage employment sc heme with bottom up planning. The 
works are identified, approved & prioritized by the  Gram Sabha at the Gram Panchayat level in 
each States/UTs including Odisha as per the provisi on of the Act. Accordingly, the action plan 
(shelf of work) of the permissible works is prepared & approved by the Gram Sabha and can be 
taken up as per the demand. The planning of works i s done as per the estimated person days to 
be generated for the work in a financial year at th e time of assessment of labour budget. There 
is no target fixed for any specific work from the M inistry, but are taken up as per the demand 
and priority of the Gram Panchayat. Hence, no work- wise allocation of funds is made. During 
current financial year 2020-21, as on 03.03.2021, t he Ministry has released Rs. 443697.98 lakh 
till now to Odisha for implementation of Scheme. Th e major category wise work status in 
Odisha under Mahatma Gandhi NREGA is given at Annexure.
